violations.rule: direct OpenAI provider endpoint (AI-provider egress class)

observations: Zeck arm: 5/5 declared corpus tasks resolved by the pinned unmodified Cline CLI with Zeck as its sole AI execution authority (act-mode-edit:resolved, plan-mode:resolved, vision-qa:resolved, reasoning-math:resolved, context-compaction:resolved).
Every corpus edge execution terminated COMPLETED with durable verification (see zeckTraces); Cline's own reported usage matched the rail-reported usage per turn.

Direct same-supply arm (no Zeck mediation): 4/4 tasks resolved; the direct arm's single text endpoint rejected the vision task's multimodal content (provider-error 1210), while the Zeck arm's rail routed the same edge to the vision surface and resolved it.

comparison.statement: Same-supply direct (non-Zeck) arm — the same pinned Cline CLI calling the same GLM supply endpoint directly with no Zeck mediation (the application holds the endpoint credential, by definition of a direct baseline): 4/4 tasks resolved vs the Zeck arm's 5/5; mean 27.0s per resolved direct outcome vs 18.0s per resolved Zeck outcome; direct-arm provider egress to the supply endpoint observed in the direct arm's egress log (present — the direct-provider call the Zeck arm provably does not make); supply-side rate-limiting observed in the direct arm (no mediation-side pacing — disclosed). Token usage per arm recorded in the battery section.
Strong optimized non-Zeck baseline (external commercial providers via OpenRouter or first-party endpoints) NOT RUN: this sandbox has no external provider credentials; owner: Lead.

The sandbox's GLM supply endpoint does not report USD prices; token usage per resolved outcome is measured and recorded (Zeck arm: 16314 in / 386 out tokens per resolved outcome; direct arm tokens in the battery section), micro-USD settlement is not (the budgets authority's reservation estimate is recorded on each execution's dispatch).

limitations.statement: The model supply for every delegated edge is the sandbox's authorized GLM endpoint (internal-api.z.ai), dispatched platform-side through the real model gateway (custom rail; the vision surface through its vision endpoint). No external AI provider was reachable or used; external-provider rails are an operator boundary, not evidence about the delegation boundary this proof tests.

The reasoning edge is exercised end-to-end at the request-control level (CLI --thinking high → wire reasoning_effort → rail thinking control → supply), and the served supply model (glm-4-plus) accepts the control but does not surface reasoning content in its responses; reasoning-output surfacing is a supply-model property, not a delegation-boundary property (disclosed).

The supply endpoint's vision surface does not execute the OpenAI tools axis (the declared vision corpus task is a final-answer task); tool-carrying vision turns would need a tool-capable vision model on the supply side — a supply-capability boundary, disclosed, not a delegation-boundary defect (the vision edge itself is delegated and resolved).

Delegated subagent/teammate loops (team tools) ride the SAME handler-factory seam as the primary agent loop and are delegated through the same adapter edge by construction (attribution: content-derived, defaulting to the act edge); the declared corpus does not spawn subagents, so no subagent-specific execution is separately evidenced.

notRunCauses.cause: No external AI-provider credentials exist in this sandbox (OpenRouter/OpenAI/Anthropic first-party endpoints are unreachable); a strong optimized non-Zeck baseline cannot be measured here.

ruleResults.detail: All 5 declared edges are delegated through Zeck (or explicitly reclassified non-AI with recorded justification).
Direct AI-provider egress is provably blocked (deny harness active, every violation blocked) during the proof.
The application remained functionally usable for the declared corpus during the proof.
All 5 delegated edge(s) correlate to Zeck execution records with durable evidence.
Every delegated edge carries live Zeck evidence from a live proof record.
